findings.issue_text: [BUG] Deleting mark_failed_threshold, create_issue_platform_occurrence, get_failure_reason, get_monitor_environment_context, SimpleCheckIn, and HUMAN_FAILURE_STATUS_MAP from mark_failed.py breaks every existing import of these public symbols without updating any callers in this diff. In-repo tests (e.g. tests/sentry/monitors/) and any other modules that import these names from sentry.monitors.logic.mark_failed raise ImportError at collection time, failing CI; the diff contains no test or caller updates to repoint them.

[ADVISORY] get_monitor_environment_context computes a modified `config` (with schedule_type converted via get_schedule_type_display) but returns `monitor_environment.monitor.config` unmodified, discarding the computed copy. Consumers of the monitor context in issue events (UI display of monitor config for incident occurrences) always receive the raw numeric schedule_type instead of the human-readable display value, so the conversion code at line 158-160 is dead work; this bug was carried over verbatim from mark_failed.py during the move.

[ADVISORY] get_failure_reason with failed_checkins whose statuses are all outside HUMAN_FAILURE_STATUS_MAP (e.g. CheckInStatus.UNKNOWN) produces an empty Counter, so sum==0 and get_text_list is called with an empty list, yielding a garbled message like " check-ins detected" instead of a fallback. Users viewing the failure-reason evidence for an incident triggered by a non-standard status see a truncated/nonsensical string; behavior is unchanged from before but the move is the natural place to guard it.

[ADVISORY] get_monitor_environment_context copies the config into `config` and replaces schedule_type on the copy, but the returned dict embeds `monitor_environment.monitor.config` (the original, unmodified dict), so the translated schedule_type display value is silently discarded. Consumers of the monitor context in issue occurrences always see the raw schedule_type (e.g. "cron" or an integer) rather than the human-readable display value; this latent bug was carried over verbatim from mark_failed.py, and the reorganization was the opportunity to fix it.

[ADVISORY] The refactor deletes the public symbols mark_failed_threshold, create_issue_platform_occurrence, get_failure_reason, get_monitor_environment_context, HUMAN_FAILURE_STATUS_MAP, SINGULAR_HUMAN_FAILURE_MAP, and the mark_failed-local SimpleCheckIn without any re-export or deprecation shim, while the diff adds no test coverage for the new modules incidents.py and incident_occurrence.py. Any out-of-tree or in-repo caller (existing tests, migration scripts, or getsentry extensions) that imports these names from sentry.monitors.logic.mark_failed now fails with ImportError; and the relocated logic in incidents.py/incident_occurrence.py ships with zero assertions of its own in this diff, so a regression in the moved code is caught only if old call-path tests survive the import breakage.

[ADVISORY] get_monitor_environment_context builds a modified copy of the monitor config (replacing schedule_type with its display value) but then returns the unmodified monitor_environment.monitor.config, so the schedule_type display conversion is silently discarded. Anyone viewing the monitor context on an incident occurrence sees the raw schedule_type value (e.g. 'crontab') instead of the human-readable display string the code clearly intends; this was carried over verbatim from the deleted mark_failed implementation, so the refactor preserved the defect in the new module rather than fixing it.

[ADVISORY] The refactor deletes the public module-level names mark_failed_threshold and create_issue_platform_occurrence from mark_failed.py without any re-export or deprecation alias, breaking any in-tree or out-of-tree importer of those symbols. Code that imported create_issue_platform_occurrence or mark_failed_threshold from sentry.monitors.logic.mark_failed (tests, tasks, or API consumers not updated in this diff) raises ImportError at import time; nothing in the diff updates any other call sites, so this rename is untraceable to a stated requirement and should either keep aliases or be verified as having no external references.

[ADVISORY] The retained import `from sentry.monitors.models import CheckInStatus, MonitorCheckIn, MonitorEnvironment` is coupled to code that was moved out: if the surviving mark_failed body no longer references CheckInStatus, the import is dead weight left behind by an incomplete move. The next reader tracing failure-threshold logic starts from mark_failed.py and finds stale imports pointing at logic that now lives in incidents.py, increasing the chance they edit or extend the wrong module; the leftover import is the residue of the migration not being traced fully.

[BUG] get_monitor_environment_context builds a normalized `config` copy (replacing schedule_type with its display value) but then returns the raw, unmodified `monitor.config` in the dict, discarding the normalized copy entirely. The `schedule_type` substitution on lines 163-165 is dead code: every occurrence produced for a monitor incident ships the raw integer schedule_type in the monitor context instead of the display string the code clearly intends, so consumers rendering the monitor context (the issue event's contexts.monitor.config) show an opaque enum int where a human-readable schedule type was meant.

[ADVISORY] The occurrence-creation loop re-fetches all threshold check-ins and calls create_incident_occurrence once per check-in, with each call independently executing get_last_successful_checkin() and producing a separate Kafka occurrence payload, even though the occurrence content is identical except for the trace_id of the triggering check-in. For a monitor with failure_issue_threshold = N, one failing check-in triggers N Kafka occurrences and N last-successful-checkin queries for a single incident; for the OK/ACTIVE path the first check-in of the window (not the triggering one) typically has no trace_id, so the trace context is dropped while N duplicate-adjacent events fan out to the issue platform, multiplying consumer load and event volume on high-churn monitors.

[ADVISORY] The OK/ACTIVE threshold check queries all check-ins with date_added__lte the failed check-in and slices to failure_issue_threshold only after the queryset is materialized via list(), rather than slicing the queryset ([:failure_issue_threshold]) in SQL. A monitor environment with months of retained check-ins reads every historical row's id/date_added/status into worker memory on each failure evaluation; slicing the queryset before list() would push the LIMIT into SQL, so the current form is an unbounded materialization on a hot path that grows linearly with check-in retention.

[ADVISORY] The refactor deletes the public names mark_failed_threshold, create_issue_platform_occurrence, and SimpleCheckIn from the mark_failed module's namespace without any deprecation shim or re-export, silently changing the module's public surface. Any in-repo or out-of-tree caller importing `from sentry.monitors.logic.mark_failed import mark_failed_threshold` (the function existed at this path before this diff) now gets an ImportError at import time — for in-repo callers a CI failure, for plugin/consumer code a hard startup failure with no signal in this diff that the symbol moved; the diff title says 'Reorganize' but does not state the API break.

[ADVISORY] get_monitor_environment_context builds a display-adjusted `config` copy (schedule_type mapped to its display value) but then returns `monitor_environment.monitor.config` verbatim, discarding the adjusted copy — behavior carried over verbatim from the deleted code, preserving the original bug rather than the apparent intent of the copy. The shipped monitor context in every incident occurrence event contains the raw numeric schedule_type instead of the human-readable display string the first four lines of the function are written to produce; whoever consumes this context (issue UI/event payload) gets the wrong value, and the dead `config` variable makes the next editor of this function likely to 'fix' the return and unknowingly change emitted payload format.

[ADVISORY] get_monitor_environment_context computes a display-transformed copy of monitor.config (schedule_type replaced with its display value) but then returns the original unmodified monitor_environment.monitor.config in the dict, so the local `config` variable is dead code and the returned context silently drops the intended schedule_type transformation. The moved code carried over a latent defect: users viewing monitor incident contexts see raw numeric schedule_type instead of the human-readable display string; the next editor who assumes the copy is used will ship a behavior change without intending one.

[BUG] try_incident_threshold fires an incident without reaching failure_issue_threshold when the monitor has fewer total check-ins than the threshold. In the threshold>1 branch, the query slices previous_checkins[:failure_issue_threshold] but never checks len(previous_checkins) >= failure_issue_threshold — a monitor whose very first check-in fails with threshold=5 produces a 1-element list containing no OK check-in, so status flips to ERROR and a MonitorIncident + occurrence are produced on check-in #1, incorrectly alerting users (and then every subsequent check-in continues generating occurrences) despite the configured threshold never being reached.

[BUG] get_monitor_environment_context computes a display-value config copy and then throws it away, returning the raw monitor.config instead. The copy at `config = monitor_environment.monitor.config.copy()` and the `schedule_type` translation to display form are dead: the returned dict at line 170 uses `monitor_environment.monitor.config` (the original), so event_data's monitor context always contains the raw numeric schedule_type instead of the human-readable display value — the evidence/context shown to users silently differs from what the code intends.

[ADVISORY] Occurrence emission is silently skipped when the active incident is missing, while the function still returns True and sends the failure signal. In the MonitorStatus.ERROR branch, `incident = monitor_env.active_incident` can be None (incident resolved/cleaned up while status lagged); the `and incident` guard then skips every create_incident_occurrence and the signal fires anyway with return True — a user whose monitor keeps failing sees no new occurrence for those check-ins and no log is emitted, leaving the gap invisible to both the user and operators debugging missing alerts.
